newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Rite Aid sees fewer deal chances.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Rite Aid sees fewer deal chances.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp Chairman Martin Grass said the company's latest acquisition of regional chains K&B Services Inc and Harco Inc represents opportunitistic transactions rather than an aggressive Southern expansion.
However, he did not rule out future purchases in the region. "We find any part of the country appealing where we can get strong market share," he said.
In a telephone interview Monday, Grass also said there would be fewer acquisition opportunities because of widespread consolidation in the drugstore industry.
Grass said the pacts to acquire the privately held chains would have a neutral effect on earnings in the short term, before becoming accretive by the second quarter of 1998.
"We don't see any dilution from the acquisition," he said.
The company did not disclose the value of the transactions, but Grass said he was comfortable with a Wall Street Journal estimate of $325 million to $340 million.
In a related matter, Grass said the company's integration of West Coast chain Thrifty PayLess Inc was ahead of schedule. Rite Aid announced the $1.3 billion acquisition in October.
Grass said there were 35 employees left in the central office of Thrifty Payless, down from 780.
"We originally had scheduled all calendar year to get integrated. Here it is July and we're just about done," he said.

The fast-moving integration of Thrifty PayLess enabled Rite Aid to pursue the latest transactions, he said. At the time of the Thrifty PayLess transaction, Grass had said he did not expect to participate in any acquisitions in 1997.
That changed when Rite Aid was approached by K&B investment bankers about a transaction and then decided to pursue Harco.
"Sometimes you have to take advantage of an opportunity when it presents itself," Grass said.
But those opportunities are growing scarce after a flood of recent deals in the fragmented industry.

"I keep saying there's less and less (opportunity)... but there obviously are some opportunities although they're getting very scarce - especially the quality of what is left. They're not necessarily all that appealing -- at least to us," said Grass, who also holds the position of chief executive officer.
Shares of Rite Aid were 7/16 higher at 48-7/16 early Monday afternoon.
